motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pass the routine consent agenda
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote; the motion does not list which items were included.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — the consent agenda is the batch of uncontested business the council passes together, and nothing in it changes anything for residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 2.15 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #59:044:0015) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 2.15 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #59:044:0015) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sell 2.15 acres of city land
motions.summary: The city approved disposing of 2.15 acres of city-owned land (Utah County parcel 59:044:0015) and set the terms; the motion names no buyer or price.
motions.impact: Unless you live next to that parcel, nothing changes for you. The land leaves city ownership under terms the council set but the motion does not spell out.

motions.item_title: Adopt an Amended Preliminary Plat for Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Amended Preliminary Plat for Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Revised layout for the Town Center Marketplace
motions.summary: The city approved an amended preliminary plat — the proposed layout of lots and streets — for the Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you today. A preliminary plat is an early planning step for the Marketplace site, well before anything gets built.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.20.020, Compensation Schedule of Statutory Officers
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.20.020, Compensation Schedule of Statutory Officers. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change the pay schedule for city officers
motions.summary: The city amended the compensation schedule for its statutory officers; the motion does not state the new pay figures.
motions.impact: This is internal city payroll housekeeping — nothing changes for residents, and the motion does not say whether the pay went up or down.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.040(E) Location of Parking Areas; and Section 17.55.100 Shared Parking and Curb Cuts with the change in 17.55.100 from 40% required shared parking to 35% required shared parking
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.040(E) Location of Parking Areas; and Section 17.55.100 Shared Parking and Curb Cuts with the change in 17.55.100 from 40% required shared parking to 35% required shared parking. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cut required shared parking from 40% to 35%
motions.summary: The city eased its parking rules, lowering required shared parking from 40% to 35% and changing where parking areas can be located on a site.
motions.impact: This lands on developers and businesses planning new projects, who now have to set aside less shared parking. Nothing changes at existing homes or businesses.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.35.050 Drive-Thru Lanes
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.35.050 Drive-Thru Lanes. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay new rules for drive-thru lanes
motions.summary: The council set aside a decision on changes to the city's rules for drive-thru lanes.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now — the existing drive-thru rules stay in place unless and until the council takes the item back up.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Sections 17.10.030 Structure Definition, and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards Table
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Sections 17.10.030 Structure Definition, and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards Table. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Tweak housing rules and the definition of a structure
motions.summary: The city changed its zoning code's definition of a "structure" and its table of residential development standards; the motion does not say what the changes were.
motions.impact: The motion gives no detail on what actually changed, so there is nothing here that tells you whether it affects what you can build on your lot. Anyone planning a project should check the updated code.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road Property and instruct Staff to return to City Council when the future property to be exchanged is determined for Council approval
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road Property and instruct Staff to return to City Council when the future property to be exchanged is determined for Council approval. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Clear the way to trade 20.35 acres by Bypass Road
motions.summary: The city approved disposing of up to 20.35 acres of city land known as the Bypass Road Property, and told staff to return once an exchange property is chosen.
motions.impact: No land has changed hands yet, and nothing changes for you today. The council still has to approve the actual swap once staff identifies what the city would get in return.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits with the change in definition stating that an athletic facility is defined as a high school or middle school regulation size soccer, football, baseball or softball field. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.. Councilmembers requested an amended motion to include the Rodeo Grounds and City owned property in the proposed amendment. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits with a change stating that an athletic facility is defined as a high school, middle school or City owned regulation size soccer, football, baseball, or softball field, or the Rodeo Grounds. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sign rules now cover school and city sports fields
motions.summary: The city rewrote its sign rules and defined an athletic facility as a regulation-size school or city-owned soccer, football, baseball or softball field, or the Rodeo Grounds.
motions.impact: This matters if you run, sponsor, or advertise at a school field, a city field, or the Rodeo Grounds — those are now the places the sign rules apply to. For most residents, nothing changes.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Delay a franchise deal with Zayo Group
motions.summary: The council put off a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, taking no action on its terms.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents right now. The agreement is set aside and would have to come back before the council for any decision.

motions.item_title: Add a funding plan for Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to the L…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add a funding plan for Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Put Airport Road funding on the state priority list
motions.summary: The council added a funding plan for roads serving the Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to the city's legislative priorities list.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This is the city telling state lawmakers what it wants money for; road work would only follow if the state actually funds it.
